mustStayConstant: benchmarks/tasks/** and benchmarks/holdout/** (task prompts, budgets, fixtures; the holdout tree hash is in benchmarks/holdout.sha256)
benchmarks/runtime workload definitions (FROZEN.json tree hash); a change needs a recorded rationale and starts a new baseline
the model id, temperature, repair and token budgets, the order and number of trials, the price table (tools/ai-eval/src/spend.ts)
the three.js baseline: its documentation (benchmarks/baselines/docs/reference.md) and task starters; it was not re-run after M7.1, so a changed baseline must be re-measured
the machine: the numbers are one Windows 11 workstation with one adapter; a different machine is a different baseline
knownIssues: CI job browser-software (Ubuntu, software renderer): specs/m4/dev-overlay.spec.ts:239 and specs/m6/getting-started.spec.ts:128 fail on most runs; both pass locally on the software project. Cause not found.
Firefox 155 (headed, WebGPU preferences): 6 failures of 251 specs (evidence/M7/environment-matrix.md); WebKit and headless Firefox expose no usable adapter.

Runtime: all seven workloads exceed the 20 % investigation threshold against direct WebGPU (benchmarks/results/runtime/report-after-quiet.md); physics, mount/reload/dispose and startup did not move with K-04.
AI: the three.js baseline is ahead on tokens per completed task in every comparison; the compiler context for cold-start tasks fills 22.6 kB of a 24 kB budget (decision 0112).
Spec versus compiler: seven places recorded by K-03 (decision 0116) and W0030 / E9010 (decisions 0102, 0103) are documented, not changed.
reading: A runtime row improves when its p95 falls on a quiet machine (median CPU load before a pass about 10 %) and the direct reference does not move with it; the direct reference moved by up to 25 % between runs (startup), so differences below that are noise.

An AI row improves when completion rises or tokens per completed task fall on the same tasks and trials; one run of 5 trials per task is the unit, and no repeat of an unchanged setup was run, so the noise floor of these rates is not measured (a rate over 170 attempts has a standard error of roughly 3.5 points, over 40 attempts about 7).
The holdout (8 tasks) was not used for design; its tasks may be easier than the main set. Do not tune against it.
